name: Lake Marian Track
why: Ten minutes to a chain of waterfalls, then a steep forest climb to an alpine lake in a hanging valley under the Darran Mountains.
book: Free, no permit. Turn off the Milford Road at Marian Corner (about 87 km from Te Anau) onto the Hollyford Road; the car park is 1 km down this gravel road.
water: Streams and the lake: treat before drinking. Nothing at the car park.
dangers: Marian Creek is fast with slippery rocks: a fall into the water can kill. Stay on the track and behind barriers at the falls.
Above the falls the track is steep, rooty and muddy.
Do not walk around the lake edge in winter and spring: avalanche paths reach the shore.
Stinging nettle (ongaonga) along the track: wear long trousers.
turnaround: If you are not at the lake 2 hours after leaving the car park, or the creek is in flood, go back down.

points.name: Lake Marian car park
points.note: On the Hollyford Road. A swing bridge crosses the Hollyford River into the forest.

points.name: Lake Marian Falls
points.note: A boardwalk to a series of falls and pools on Marian Creek, 10 minutes in. The tramping track starts here.

points.name: Lake Marian
points.note: An alpine lake above the bushline, ringed by peaks of the Darran Mountains; reflections on a calm day. Return the same way.
